citations.quote: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). For every compact collared triad $(W;M_0,M_1)$ there are an adapted excellent Morse function $f:W\to[0,1]$ and an adapted complete downward gradient-like field $X$, both agreeing with the product model on smaller neighborhoods in the fixed collars: $f=t_0/3$ near $M_0$, $f=1-t_1/3$ near $M_1$, and $X$ is its negative Riemannian gradient for a metric that is a product metric there. Here **adapted complete** has the collar-extension meaning of [[def-morse-function-adapted-to-a-cobordism]]: $X$ is the restriction of a complete smooth field on a boundaryless collar extension of $W$; a trajectory is followed in $W$ only until it exits a face.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On a compact collared triad $(W;M_0,M_1)$, every adapted excellent Morse function determines a finite handle decomposition relative to $M_0$, with one handle of index $\operatorname{ind}(p)$ per critical point. Given an adapted field, the attaching sphere is the boundary of its local unstable disk transported to the lower regular level. Conversely every finite handle decomposition relative to $M_0$ is realized by an adapted excellent Morse function with one critical point per handle, of the same index, ordered by the prescribed handle order.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $X$ be a complete downward gradient-like field
for a smooth function $f$ on a smooth manifold, let $f^{-1}[a,b]$ be a compact
regular band, and let $h_t$, $t\in[0,1]$, be a smooth isotopy of $f^{-1}(b)$
with $h_0=\mathrm{id}$ whose support is contained in a compact subset. Then
there is a complete downward gradient-like field $X'$ for $f$, equal to $X$
outside $f^{-1}(a,b)$, such that the diffeomorphism
$f^{-1}(a)\to f^{-1}(b)$ obtained by following $X'$-trajectories backwards equals
$h_1\circ\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the corresponding diffeomorphism for $X$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $f$ be adapted on a compact triad with adapted
field $X$, let $P$ (value $c$) and $Q$ (value $c'>c$) be consecutive critical
levels, and let $v\in(c,c')$ be regular. Let $D_q$ be the local unstable disk of
$q\in Q$ and $E_p$ the local stable disk of $p\in P$, provided by the local
stable/unstable manifold theorem. Then:

1. for every $q\in Q$ the set of points in which the trajectories through $D_q$
   cross $f^{-1}(v)$ is a compact embedded sphere $A_q$ of dimension
   $\operatorname{ind}(q)-1$, and for every $p\in P$ the crossing set $B_p$ of
   the trajectories through $E_p$ is a compact embedded sphere of dimension
   $n-\operatorname{ind}(p)-1$, with the convention $S^{-1}=\varnothing$, so
   these spheres are empty when the index is $0$, respectively $n$;
2. for $n\ge1$, each $A_q$ and $B_p$ has a product neighbourhood in the
   closed $(n-1)$-manifold $f^{-1}(v)$, transported by the normalized flow
   from the local model; for $n=0$, the regular fibre and all crossing
   sets are empty, their product-neighbourhood maps are the unique empty
   maps, and no manifold of dimension $-1$ is asserted;
3. a trajectory whose limits lie in $Q$ and $P$ crosses $f^{-1}(v)$ exactly
   once, at a point of $A_q\cap B_p$, and every such intersection point lies on
   such a trajectory.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(f,X)$ be adapted on a compact triad, and choose regular $0<u<c<c'<v<1$ such that the critical set in $K=f^{-1}[u,v]$ consists exactly of finite clusters $P,Q$ at values $c,c'$. Suppose there is no $X$-trajectory from a point of $Q$ to a point of $P$. Then for any $a,a'\in(u,v)$, including $a>a'$ or $a=a'$, there is an adapted Morse $g$ with the same critical points and indices as $f$, $g=a$ on $P$, $g=a'$ on $Q$, and $X$ still downward gradient-like for $g$. The function is $f$ outside the interior of $K$ and near its two end levels, and is $f$ plus a constant near every critical point. On a triad with just these two critical clusters, one may also use its face levels as $u,v$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a nonempty compact connected triad with
$M_0\ne\varnothing$ connected. Then $W$ admits a handle decomposition relative
to $M_0$ with no $0$-handles. If $M_0$ has $k$ components the same argument
leaves no $0$-handles and begins with $k-1$ connecting $1$-handles; if
$M_0=\varnothing$, exactly the $0$-handles needed to create the components of
$W$ remain, one per component.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be a connected smooth $n$-manifold with
nonempty boundary and let $D\subseteq\partial N$ be an embedded closed disk.
Then the boundary connected sum $N\natural D^n$, obtained by gluing an $n$-disk
along $D$, is diffeomorphic to $N$ by a diffeomorphism equal to the identity
outside a collar neighbourhood of $D$.

derivations.claim: Prescribe the function to be $t$ on the vertical collar, the inward height on $A_0$ and one minus the inward height on $A_1$. These prescriptions agree on their product corner charts by the hypothesis. Smooth patching here is finite: restrict Euclidean chart bumps to the half-spaces and quadrants of those charts, extend by zero beyond their strict support margins, and divide by their positive finite sum near the compact boundary. Patch the prescribed height with the constant $1/2$ only beyond smaller boundary collars. The resulting $h:M\to[0,1]$ has the required endpoint fibers and has no critical point near any boundary face or corner. Thus every possible critical point is in a compact subset of the ordinary interior.

On that compact subset apply the actual finite differential perturbation of [F1]: choose finitely many interior charts and bumps $\chi_j$, equal to one on smaller charts covering it, and perturb by $\sum a_{jk}\chi_j x_j^k$. At each possible zero the parameter differentials span the cotangent fiber, so the evaluation is transverse to the zero section. A sufficiently small good parameter exists by [F1]; compact value margins retain the endpoint fibers and smaller parameters retain nonvanishing on the transition collar. Its critical points are nondegenerate and finite. Distinct small constant bumps near those points separate their values without changing their Hessians or the protected collars. Patch Euclidean metrics in the Morse charts and the metric $dt^2+dr^2+g_B$ near the vertical face, using the same finite partition construction; here $r$ is the inward vertical-face collar coordinate. The negative gradient has the exact Morse models and equals $-\partial_t$ on that collar. Extend the field to signed face and corner charts and cut it off on a boundaryless carrier, as in the actual completeness construction of [F1]. This gives complete ambient trajectories restricted to $M$ until horizontal exit.

An interior trajectory cannot enter the protected vertical collar from its interior edge and then approach its vertical boundary: in a smaller product strip its $r$ coordinate is constant because the field is $-\partial_t$. A trajectory meeting that smaller strip stays in it until horizontal exit in both time directions and cannot have an interior critical limit. Therefore all critical crossing spheres and their regular-band transports are compact subsets of horizontal interiors away from a smaller fixed strip. On a compact regular band, strict descent away from the finite Morse blocks has a positive lower bound; the exact exponential flow in each block accounts for possible infinite-time limits only at its critical point. Finite regular transports thus exist until the next prescribed level. Applying the local block and regular-band constructions of [F3] in those interior charts gives a handle presentation with the prescribed boundary maps, and with all attaching thickenings away from the vertical strip. This proves the relative-face handle construction without applying an ordinary closed-face theorem to the corners.

Consider a strict index inversion at two consecutive critical values: the lower point $p$ has index larger than the higher point $q$. The crossing sets at an intermediate level have the dimensions in [F3]. If $\operatorname{ind}(q)=0$ or $\operatorname{ind}(p)=3$, one set is empty. The only other possibility is $\operatorname{ind}(p)=2$, $\operatorname{ind}(q)=1$, when both sets are finite point sets on a two-dimensional regular level. Move one of these finite sets off the other by arbitrarily small translations in disjoint coordinate disks around its points, keeping the disks inside the level interior. The cut-off constant translation fields give a smooth level isotopy supported in those disks. Use the actual regular-band shear of [F3], supported between two nearby regular levels in this interior, to change the field so the crossing sets become disjoint. Nothing changes on the vertical strip or near the critical blocks. A trajectory connecting $q$ to $p$ would cross that intermediate level in both sets, so no such trajectory remains. This is the entire dimension-specific separation argument; no positive-dimensional crossing sphere must be moved off another one for a strict inversion.

The critical-trajectory compactness and orbit-separation construction in [F4] applies inside this band with its two critical blocks. Indeed a limiting regular path either has bounded travel time away from those blocks or breaks at one of the two critical points, by their exact exponential equations; a broken connection between the two is excluded by step 4.1. Those compact trajectory sets miss the protected product strip by step 3.1. On the lower regular level choose an additional bump equal to one near their compact exits and zero near the vertical boundary, and extend it constantly along regular trajectories. Near each critical-trajectory set extend it constantly as one; exit continuity in the block model makes this extension smooth, just as for the orbit-separating function $\beta$ in [F4]. At a local minimum use the constant-one extension on its attracting neighborhood with no lower through-exit, and reverse this argument at a maximum. This supplies a smooth orbit-constant $\alpha$ equal to one near the critical sets and zero near the vertical strip. If $G(f,\beta)$ is the value interchange from [F4], use $g=(1-\alpha)f+\alpha G(f,\beta)$. Since $d\alpha(X)=d\beta(X)=0$, its derivative along the field is $dg(X)=(1-\alpha+\alpha\partial_1G)df(X)<0$ off the critical points. Near those points it is the prescribed constant value change, while it is exactly the old height on the boundary strip and near the band's end levels. This interchanges the inverted values without new critical points or boundary changes.

Repeat steps 4.1–5.1 for adjacent strict index inversions. The inversion count of the finite index list decreases by one at every adjacent exchange, so this terminates with all zero-handles first, then all one-handles, then all two-handles and finally all three-handles. Keep the critical values distinct within each group. Local Morse and regular-band blocks give the index-ordered relative presentation on the same manifold with its original boundary identifications. There is no need to merge equal-index critical values or to appeal to a higher-dimensional version of the face argument.

In that ordered presentation form the finite graph whose vertices are the components of the incoming collar and the new zero-handle balls, with the one-handles as edges. This graph is connected because handles of index at least two have connected attaching regions and cannot join components. Root a spanning tree at any incoming component, which exists because $A_0$ is nonempty. Process its edges outward: absorb every newly reached bare ball and its incident one-handle by [F5], retaining an edge when it joins another incoming component. All disks and collars of these operations lie in compact horizontal interiors, so the vertical strip is untouched. Transport all remaining attaching maps through each absorption; this removes every zero-handle while preserving the actual boundary parametrizations as presentation data. Reverse the presentation from the nonempty outgoing face and apply the same procedure, using its possibly several collar components. In the original direction this removes only three-handles and their paired two-handles and cannot recreate a zero-handle. Reversing back gives only one- and two-handles, with every one-handle still before every two-handle. The supported absorptions and all transported maps retain the originally specified horizontal and vertical identifications, as asserted.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 1.1 and 5.1 allow an empty vertical face; step6.1 allows an empty critical list.
Steps 6.1–7.1 allow zero one-handles or zero two-handles, including a product cobordism.
Steps 4.1–5.1 treat one adjacent inverted critical pair.

boundaries.reason: Smooth product corners and nonempty horizontal faces are supplied; step2.1 makes critical points nondegenerate.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 1.1,5.1 and7.1 retain prescribed horizontal/vertical boundary parameterizations and fixed vertical heights.
Step 2.1 uses countable choice only through the stated Morse and supported-flow suppliers; chart, parameter and tree choices after compactness are finite.

axioms.use: Countable choice is inherited from smooth Morse perturbation, supported flows, critical-value interchange and disk absorption. All charts, critical points, index exchanges and tree absorptions are finite.

risk_review.notes: New3Dface construction is explicit. Strict-index separation in step4.1 requires only finite point sets on a2Dlevel; orbit cutoff in step5.1 preserves all vertical heights. No d>=4Statement is applied in dimension3; no fundamental-group or Whitney-trick assumption is imported.

lem-three-dimensional-relative-face-hand.proof_status_evidence: Seven literal steps and scoped successful checks; actual ordinary Morse, local moving-off, orbit-interchange and disk-absorption proofs read. Independent owner review remains owed.
